card.statement:
The group scheme $(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a connected reductive group, $T^{\vee}_{\mathbf{k}}$ is a maximal torus of this group, and the root datum of $(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})_{\mathrm{red}}$ with respect to $T^{\vee}_{\mathbf{k}}$ is dual to that of $(G,T)$ .

Note that Proposition 14.5 is sufficient to complete the program outlined in §14.1. Indeed,
once this result is proved, we will know that the group scheme $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}_{p}}$ over $\mathbf{Z}_{p}$ satisfies the following conditions:

•

$\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}_{p}}$ is affine and flat over $\mathbf{Z}_{p}$ (see §14.2);

•

the generic fiber $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Q}_{p}}=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{Q}_{p})\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{Z}_{p})}\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}_{p}}$ is connected and smooth over $\mathbf{Q}_{p}$ (see Theorem 9.8);

•

the reduced geometric special fiber $(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})_{\mathrm{red}}=(\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{k})\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{Z}_{p})}\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}_{p}})_{\mathrm{red}}$ is of finite type over $\mathbf{k}$ (see Lemma 14.2) and its identity component $(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})_{\mathrm{red}}^{\circ}$ is a reductive group of the same dimension as $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Q}_{p}}$ (see Proposition 14.5).

In the terminology of [PY], this means that $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}_{p}}$ is quasi-reductive. We will also know that

•

the root data of $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Q}_{p}}$ and $(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})_{\mathrm{red}}^{\circ}$ coincide.

By [PY, Theorem 1.2], it will follow that $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{Z}_{p}}$ is a reductive group over $\mathbf{Z}_{p}$ .
This will imply in particular that $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ is reduced, hence that in Proposition 14.5 we can omit the subscript “ $\mathrm{red}$ ,” and thus will finally prove the properties (2)–(4) of §14.1.

The proof of Proposition 14.5 will be based on the same ideas as in
Section 9, but with many additional difficulties.
We need some preparatory lemmas.
We denote by $R$ the quotient of $(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})_{\mathrm{red}}$ by its unipotent radical. Then the composition $T^{\vee}_{\mathbf{k}}\to(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})_{\mathrm{red}}\to R$ is injective, so that we can also consider $T^{\vee}_{\mathbf{k}}$ as a closed subgroup of $R$ .
card.label: Proposition 14.5

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
